To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Skyrme pseudo-potential is a good approximation to the nuclear interaction, but that its parameters cannot be determined with high accuracy, because the energy density functional is not sufficiently sensitive to the parameters.

the error of the Skyrmedependent part of the nuclear energy is of the order of 1-2 MeV/nucleon, and that the error of thenuclear energy due to the uncertainty of the Skyrmenuclear matter parameters is of the orderof 0.5 MeV/nucle on.
the Skyrme interaction is a very successful model of the nuclear force and that the Skyrmes N2LO potential provides a good starting point for the description of nuclei.

the development of a new class of nuclear potentials for describing nuclear structure and reactions, based on the Skyrme energy functional.
the development of the Skyrma model and the study of the properties of its soliton solutions.
a systematic analysis of the parameters in the Skyrme functional, and their impact on the properties of finite nuclei and the nuclear matter equation of state.

there is no evidence of a new physics beyond the Standard Model in the LHC data so far.
the N2LO chiral effective field theory is the best available model to describe the properties of nuclear matter.

the Skyrme interaction, with its many adjustable parameters, is not able to describe simultaneously the ground state properties of finite nuclei as well as nuclear matter and neutron matter properties in a fully satisfactory way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the N2LO chiral EFT interaction is a good starting point for the description of the properties of light nuclei.
the N2LO chiral effective field theory (EFT) is the best available framework for nuclear structure calculations.
the N2LO Skyrme interaction is a viable alternative to more complicated interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown how to construct a Skyrme model with a realistic nuclear force, that is, a model that reproduces nuclear matter properties, and which is also consistent with the properties of the pion, the nucleon, and the Delta baryon.

, while the N3LO Skyrme pseudo-potential is not a good choice for the description of the properties of the lightest nucleus in nature, it can be used to describe the properties of heavier nuclei with good accuracy.

the Skyrme force is a good approximation for the NLO chiral force in a wide range of densities, and that it can be used to study neutron star properties in the same spirit as the NLO force, which is computationally much more expensive.
